settings.label: API key
settings.meaning: Authenticates the backend to the Paddle API (Bearer). Its prefix says which environment it is for: pdl_live_apikey_ calls https://api.paddle.com, pdl_sdbx_apikey_ calls https://sandbox-api.paddle.com, and a key only works in its own environment.
settings.whereToFind: Paddle › My account › Settings › Authentication › API keys › New API key, with the customer, price, product, subscription, transaction, adjustment, customer portal session and usage event permissions the app uses. Test is a separate sandbox account (sandbox-vendors.paddle.com) with its own keys. Keys expire: 90 days by default, a year at most.

test.because: This is a live Paddle API key; the test environment uses a sandbox key (pdl_sdbx_apikey_…).

production.because: This is a sandbox Paddle API key; production needs a live key (pdl_live_apikey_…).

settings.label: Client-side token
settings.meaning: Initializes Paddle.js in the browser, which opens the checkout. Safe to publish; it can't call the API. test_ tokens are for the sandbox, live_ tokens for live.
settings.whereToFind: Paddle › My account › Settings › Authentication › Client-side tokens › New client-side token, in the sandbox account for test.

test.because: This is a live client-side token; the test environment uses a sandbox token (test_…).

production.because: This is a sandbox client-side token; production needs a live token (live_…).

settings.label: Webhook secret key
settings.meaning: The notification destination's secret key, which signs every webhook Paddle sends to it. Each destination has its own.
settings.whereToFind: Paddle › Events › Notifications › (your destination) › Edit destination › Secret key. The sandbox account's destination has its own key.

settings.label: Environment
settings.meaning: sandbox or production. Only needed for an API key made before 6 May 2025, which has no pdl_ prefix to tell; with a prefixed key it must agree with the prefix.
settings.whereToFind: sandbox for a key from the sandbox account, production for a live one. Leave it unset for a pdl_ key.

settings.label: Payment page
settings.meaning: The app's page that loads Paddle.js, on a domain Paddle approved. A checkout's url is this page with ?_ptxn=<transaction id>, and Paddle.js opens the checkout there. Unset: the account's default payment link.
settings.whereToFind: Paddle › Checkout › Checkout configuration › Default payment link, or another page on a website approved under Paddle › My account › Settings › Website approval.

operations.name: customers.create
operations.purpose: Creates a customer. Paddle keeps one customer per email address and takes no idempotency key: a repeat answers customer_already_exists.

operations.name: customers.get
operations.purpose: Reads a customer.

operations.name: customers.update
operations.purpose: Changes a customer's email, name, status or custom data.

operations.name: customers.list
operations.purpose: Lists customers, here by exact email address and status.

operations.name: customers.creditBalances
operations.purpose: A customer's credit balance in each currency: available, reserved and used.

operations.name: customerPortalSessions.create
operations.purpose: Signed-in links to the Paddle-hosted customer portal for a customer, optionally deep links for some of their subscriptions. Temporary: never stored.

operations.name: prices.list
operations.purpose: Lists the catalog's prices, with their products, a page at a time.

operations.name: subscriptions.list
operations.purpose: Lists a customer's subscriptions, a page at a time.

operations.name: subscriptions.get
operations.purpose: Reads a subscription, with its temporary management links.

operations.name: subscriptions.update
operations.purpose: Replaces a subscription's items (the complete list) with a proration billing mode, changes its custom data, or removes a scheduled change.

operations.name: subscriptions.previewUpdate
operations.purpose: What an update would bill, now and at the next renewal, without making it.

operations.name: subscriptions.cancel
operations.purpose: Cancels a subscription at the end of the billing period (a scheduled change) or immediately.

operations.name: subscriptions.pause
operations.purpose: Pauses a subscription at the end of the billing period or immediately.

operations.name: subscriptions.resume
operations.purpose: Resumes a paused subscription, immediately or on a date.

operations.name: transactions.create
operations.purpose: Creates an automatically-collected transaction for a checkout. Its checkout.url is the payment page with ?_ptxn=<id>; completing it creates the subscription for recurring items. No idempotency key: a repeat makes another unpaid transaction.

operations.name: transactions.list
operations.purpose: Lists a customer's transactions (Paddle's invoices and payments), 30 a page.

operations.name: transactions.get
operations.purpose: Reads a transaction, optionally with the totals of its adjustments.

operations.name: transactions.invoice
operations.purpose: A link to the transaction's invoice PDF, for billed or completed transactions. The link expires after an hour.

operations.name: adjustments.create
operations.purpose: Refunds all of a completed transaction or some of its items. Most live refunds wait for Paddle's approval. No idempotency key, so it is retried only when rate-limited.

operations.name: usageEvents.create
operations.purpose: Records metered usage (early access). Paddle counts each event once per customer and action by its event_key and occurred_at, so a resend with both unchanged is safe.

operations.name: eventTypes.list
operations.purpose: Lists the event types: an authenticated call that changes nothing, for a health check.

signature.description: The header is ts=<Unix seconds>;h1=<hex>, with more than one h1 while a secret is rotated. Each h1 is the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the destination's secret key as-is, of the ts value, a colon and the raw request body. Reject a ts more than five seconds from now (Paddle's own tolerance), and deduplicate on the body's event_id.

events.meaning: A customer was created, by the API or at checkout.
A checkout for recurring items completed and made a subscription.
A subscription is in a trial.
A subscription changed: items, a scheduled change, billing details or status.
A renewal payment failed and the subscription is in dunning.
A transaction was paid and processed: a checkout, a renewal or a charge.
A payment attempt on a transaction failed.
A refund, credit or chargeback was made against a transaction.
An adjustment changed status: a refund approved or rejected.
A price was added to the catalog.
A price changed or was archived.
